name: Adonijah declares himself king
summary: As David grows old, his son Adonijah exalts himself as the next king and wins the backing of Joab, David's army commander, and Abiathar the priest, while Zadok, Benaiah, and Nathan refuse to support him.

name: Nathan and Bathsheba persuade David to crown Solomon
summary: The prophet Nathan alerts Bathsheba that Adonijah has claimed the throne, and together they remind David of his oath that Solomon would reign after him, moving David to swear that Solomon will be king.

name: Solomon anointed king at Gihon
summary: David orders Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to anoint Solomon king at Gihon; when Adonijah's supporters hear the news and scatter, Adonijah flees to the altar for refuge and Solomon spares his life.

name: David charges Solomon before he dies
summary: On his deathbed, David charges Solomon to walk faithfully in God's ways and to deal wisely with Joab, reward Barzillai's sons, and bring Shimei's curse against David to account, then dies after forty years as king.

name: Solomon executes Adonijah for requesting Abishag
summary: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request Abishag, David's former attendant, as his wife; Solomon takes this as a renewed claim on the throne and has Benaiah execute Adonijah.

name: Solomon removes Abiathar, Joab, and Shimei
summary: Solomon exiles Abiathar from the priesthood, has Benaiah kill Joab at the altar and Shimei for breaking his house arrest, and replaces them with Zadok and Benaiah, firmly establishing his kingdom.

name: Solomon asks God for wisdom at Gibeon
summary: God appears to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and offers to grant any request; Solomon asks for an understanding mind to govern rather than wealth or long life, so God grants him wisdom plus riches and honor besides.

name: Solomon judges between two women over a living child
summary: Two women who share a house each claim the same surviving baby as their own; Solomon orders the child cut in two, and the true mother's plea to spare him instead reveals which woman is really his mother.

name: Solomon organizes his officials and twelve district governors
summary: Solomon appoints a council of chief officials over his kingdom and divides the land into twelve districts, each governor responsible for supplying the royal household's provisions for one month of the year.

name: Solomon's wisdom exceeds every nation
summary: Solomon speaks three thousand proverbs and composes over a thousand songs, and his wisdom about plants and animals draws visitors and kings from every nation who have heard of it.

name: Solomon and Hiram of Tyre exchange timber for food
summary: Solomon asks Hiram, king of Tyre, for cedar and cypress logs to build the temple; Hiram supplies the timber in exchange for wheat and oil, and Solomon conscripts a massive labor force of Israelite and foreign workers.

name: Solomon builds the temple over seven years
summary: In the fourth year of his reign, Solomon begins building the temple in Jerusalem, a cedar-lined structure with an inner sanctuary overlaid in gold and carved with cherubim and palm trees, finishing it seven years later.

name: The LORD promises to dwell among Israel if Solomon obeys
summary: While the temple is under construction, the LORD tells Solomon that he will fulfill his promise to David and dwell among the people of Israel, but only if Solomon walks in his statutes and keeps his commandments.

name: Solomon builds his own palace
summary: Solomon spends thirteen years constructing his own palace complex, including the Hall of the Forest of Lebanon and a hall for judgment, built of costly stone and cedar.

name: Hiram the craftsman casts the temple's bronze furnishings
summary: Solomon brings in Hiram, a skilled bronze craftsman from Tyre, who casts two great pillars for the temple's entrance and a huge round basin called the sea, set on twelve bronze oxen, along with stands and other furnishings.

name: The ark enters the temple in a cloud of glory
summary: Priests carry the ark of the covenant into the temple's inner sanctuary beneath the wings of the cherubim, and the LORD's glory fills the temple as a cloud so thick the priests cannot continue ministering.

name: Solomon dedicates the temple with a prayer
summary: Solomon blesses the assembly and prays that God will hear the prayers of Israel, and even of foreigners, offered toward the temple in times of defeat, drought, famine, and exile.

name: Israel sacrifices and feasts for seven days
summary: Solomon and all Israel offer twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred twenty thousand sheep as peace offerings, then celebrate the temple's dedication with a seven-day feast before returning home.

name: The LORD warns Solomon a second time
summary: After the temple and palace are finished, the LORD appears to Solomon again, warning that if he or his sons turn to other gods, Israel will be cut off from the land and the temple will become a ruin.

name: Solomon's fleet sails to Ophir for gold
summary: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in Galilee as payment, conscripts forced labor for his building projects, and builds a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber that, with Hiram's sailors, brings back gold from Ophir.

name: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions
summary: The queen of Sheba travels to Jerusalem with camels of spices, gold, and precious stones to test Solomon with hard questions, and after seeing his wisdom and wealth firsthand she declares that not even half of it had been told to her.

name: Solomon's gold, throne, and fleets exceed every king
summary: Solomon receives 666 talents of gold a year, builds a great ivory throne overlaid with gold, and maintains trading fleets that bring gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks every three years, making him richer than any king on earth.

name: Solomon's foreign wives turn his heart to other gods
summary: Solomon loves many foreign women, including seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and in his old age they turn his heart to worship Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh, and Molech, provoking the LORD to anger.

name: The LORD raises up adversaries against Solomon
summary: Angry at Solomon's unfaithfulness, the LORD raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Damascus as foreign adversaries, and Jeroboam, one of Solomon's own officials, as an adversary from within.

name: Ahijah promises Jeroboam ten tribes, and Solomon dies
summary: The prophet Ahijah meets Jeroboam on the road, tears his new cloak into twelve pieces, and gives him ten as a sign that God will give him ten tribes after Solomon's death; Solomon reigns forty years before he dies.

name: Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice at Shechem
summary: When Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten the heavy burdens Solomon placed on them, he rejects the elders' advice to be gracious and instead follows the young men's advice to answer even more harshly.

name: Israel rebels and makes Jeroboam king over the north
summary: Israel rejects Rehoboam's harsh rule, and only Judah and Benjamin remain loyal to the house of David; the rest of the tribes make Jeroboam king over the newly divided northern kingdom.

name: Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan
summary: Fearing that pilgrimages to Jerusalem's temple will win his people back to Rehoboam, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan and appoints priests who are not Levites to serve them.

name: A man of God confronts Jeroboam's altar at Bethel
summary: A man of God from Judah cries out against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, and it splits apart as a sign; when Jeroboam's hand withers for trying to seize him, the man of God prays and it is healed.

name: An old prophet deceives the man of God, and a lion kills him
summary: An old prophet living in Bethel falsely claims an angel told him to feed the man of God, who eats and drinks against the LORD's direct command; on the road afterward, a lion kills him for his disobedience.

name: Ahijah pronounces judgment on Jeroboam's house
summary: Jeroboam sends his wife in disguise to ask the blind prophet Ahijah about their sick son; Ahijah recognizes her anyway and pronounces the destruction of Jeroboam's house, and the boy dies the moment she returns home.

name: Shishak of Egypt plunders the temple under Rehoboam
summary: During Rehoboam's reign in Judah, Egypt's king Shishak invades Jerusalem and carries off the treasures of the temple and palace, including Solomon's gold shields, which Rehoboam replaces with bronze ones.

name: Asa reforms Judah and removes his grandmother's idol
summary: Asa becomes king of Judah after his father Abijam, removes his grandmother Maacah as queen mother for making an idol, and removes the male cult prostitutes and idols his fathers had made.

name: Baasha assassinates Nadab and wipes out Jeroboam's house
summary: Baasha assassinates Jeroboam's son Nadab and seizes the throne of Israel, then kills every remaining member of Jeroboam's family, fulfilling Ahijah's earlier prophecy against the house.

name: Zimri assassinates Elah and burns himself in the palace
summary: Zimri assassinates Baasha's son Elah while he is drinking and seizes the throne, but when Israel's army makes Omri king instead, Zimri burns the palace down around himself after just seven days as king.

name: Omri builds Samaria as Israel's capital
summary: Omri defeats his rivals to secure the throne, then buys a hill and builds Samaria, naming it after its former owner and making it Israel's new capital.

name: Ahab marries Jezebel and builds an altar to Baal
summary: Omri's son Ahab becomes king, marries Jezebel of Sidon, and builds a temple and altar to Baal in Samaria, doing more to provoke the LORD than any king of Israel before him.

name: Elijah announces a drought and is fed by ravens
summary: Elijah tells Ahab there will be no rain except at his word, then hides at the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and meat each morning and evening until the brook dries up.

name: The widow of Zarephath's flour and oil never run out
summary: Elijah asks a poor widow in Zarephath to feed him first, promising her jar of flour and jug of oil will not run out; the miracle sustains her household through the rest of the famine.

name: Elijah revives the widow's son
summary: When the widow's son stops breathing, Elijah carries him to his room, stretches himself on the boy three times in prayer, and the LORD restores the child's life.

name: Obadiah reveals he hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel
summary: Ahab's official Obadiah, secretly loyal to the LORD, tells Elijah that he hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets in caves and fed them during Jezebel's purge.

name: Elijah defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
summary: Elijah challenges four hundred fifty prophets of Baal to a contest on Mount Carmel; after their all-day pleading brings no answer, Elijah soaks his own altar in water and prays once, and fire falls and consumes the sacrifice.

name: Elijah's prayer ends the drought with rain
summary: After the prophets of Baal are killed at the brook Kishon, Elijah prays on Mount Carmel, and after his servant sees a small cloud rise from the sea seven times, a great rain ends the three-year drought.

name: Elijah flees Jezebel and is fed by an angel
summary: Frightened by Jezebel's threat to kill him, Elijah flees into the wilderness and asks God to let him die, but an angel wakes him twice with bread and water for the journey ahead.

name: The LORD speaks to Elijah in a low whisper at Horeb
summary: At Mount Horeb, Elijah complains that he alone remains faithful, and the LORD passes by not in a great wind, an earthquake, or a fire, but in a low whisper, and tells him seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal.

name: Elijah calls Elisha to follow him
summary: The LORD sends Elijah to anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha; Elijah finds Elisha plowing and throws his cloak over him, and Elisha leaves his oxen to follow Elijah as his attendant.

name: Ahab defeats Ben-hadad's siege of Samaria
summary: Syria's king Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and makes escalating demands; when a prophet promises victory, a small force of district officers routs Ben-hadad's army, and he escapes on horseback.

name: Ahab defeats Ben-hadad again the next spring
summary: Ben-hadad returns the next year with a larger army, but Israel defeats a hundred thousand Syrian foot soldiers in one day, and a collapsing wall in Aphek kills thousands more of his men.

name: Ahab spares Ben-hadad and a prophet condemns him
summary: Ben-hadad surrenders and calls Ahab his brother, and Ahab lets him go in exchange for restored cities and trading rights; an unnamed prophet then condemns Ahab for releasing a man devoted to destruction.

name: Naboth refuses to sell his vineyard to Ahab
summary: Ahab offers to buy or trade for Naboth's vineyard next to the palace, but Naboth refuses to give up his family's inheritance, and Ahab sulks and refuses to eat.

name: Jezebel arranges Naboth's death by false witnesses
summary: Jezebel writes letters in Ahab's name ordering city officials to seat false witnesses who accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king; Naboth is stoned to death, and Ahab takes possession of his vineyard.

name: Elijah confronts Ahab, who then humbles himself
summary: Elijah meets Ahab at the vineyard and pronounces the LORD's judgment on his and Jezebel's house; Ahab tears his clothes and fasts in mourning, so the LORD delays the disaster until after his death.

name: Micaiah alone predicts Ahab's defeat
summary: Before Ahab and Jehoshaphat march on Ramoth-gilead, four hundred prophets promise victory, but Micaiah alone predicts Israel will be scattered like sheep without a shepherd, and Ahab has him imprisoned for it.

name: Ahab dies in battle at Ramoth-gilead
summary: Ahab disguises himself for battle, but a random arrow strikes him between the joints of his armor, and he dies in his chariot that evening as the battle continues around him.

name: Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah's reigns are summarized
summary: Jehoshaphat reigns righteously over Judah for twenty-five years, though the high places remain, while Ahab's son Ahaziah becomes king of Israel and follows his parents into the worship of Baal.
